en.commentary:
Buying a CPAP in 2026 starts with a fact that most published rankings still skip. Philips Respironics has been barred from selling new CPAP and BiPAP machines in the United States since the consent decree was entered on 9 April 2024, and the decree runs five years before the company can even petition the court for release. That puts the earliest possible return in 2029. Philips held roughly 37% of the US sleep apnea device market in 2020, so a third of the category walked off the shelf. Any list that still puts a DreamStation at the top is describing a market that closed two years ago. Everything I rank here is a machine you can put in a cart today.

The second thing worth understanding is the price structure, because this category has an unusual one. A DME supplier billing through insurance commonly books an AirSense 11 at around $1,800. ResMed sells the same machine on its own store for $1,054, and cash retailers land between $900 and $1,100. The average private plan deductible passed $1,700 in 2026, so a reader who has not touched their deductible pays the higher of those two numbers and takes on compliance monitoring with it, four hours a night across 70% of nights in the qualifying window. Paying cash drops the monitoring requirement and usually costs less. Medicare is the clean exception: the 2026 Part B deductible is $283 and coverage picks up 80% after that, which makes insurance the better route for anyone on it.

The third thing is that the blower is the small expense. Mask cushions go every two to four weeks, tubing every three months, disposable filters every month. At cash prices that runs about $300 to $800 a year, and following the full Medicare replacement schedule it reaches roughly $1,058. Five years of supplies costs more than any single machine on this list. That is why I weighted hose and mask freedom so heavily. A machine with a standard 22mm fitting lets you shop the entire mask market and switch brands the moment a cushion stops sealing. A proprietary tube ties your supply spending to one vendor for as long as you own the device.

Every machine here requires a prescription in the United States, and any seller shipping without one is worth avoiding. This page compares products, prices and availability. Pressure settings, mode selection and any question about Zepbound belong with a sleep physician.

highlights.title: The ResMed AirSense 11 earns the top spot on availability and mask freedom
highlights.body: I keep landing on the AirSense 11 because it wins the two things that decide long-term cost. It takes a standard 22mm hose, which means every mask on the market fits and you can change brands the week a cushion stops sealing for you. And ResMed publishes a cash price of $1,054 on its own store, which gives every reader a hard number to hold a DME quote against. The AutoSet algorithm has a decade of field data behind it, myAir puts usage hours and AHI on the phone every morning, and the humidifier and heated tube are one assembly with two water paths to clean. At $1,054 it is the most expensive machine I would call a default recommendation, and the mask ecosystem alone justifies the gap over the $599 tier.

highlights.title: Paying cash beats running a CPAP through commercial insurance for most people, and the gap is wide
highlights.body: Here is the arithmetic that changed how I rank this category. A DME supplier billing insurance commonly books an AirSense 11 near $1,800. The same machine is $1,054 direct from ResMed and $900 to $1,100 from cash retailers. The average 2026 private plan deductible is above $1,700, so a reader who has not met it pays the inflated number in full. Insurance also brings compliance monitoring, four hours a night across 70% of nights in the qualifying period, and a supplier can stop paying or reclaim the device when those numbers slip. Cash purchase removes both the markup and the monitoring. Medicare runs the other way: with a $283 Part B deductible and 80% coverage after it, insurance is the right route for anyone enrolled.

highlights.title: Five years of cushions and tubing cost more than the machine, so buy the hose fitting first
highlights.body: Mask cushions get replaced every two to four weeks, tubing every three months, disposable filters every month, humidifier chambers every six. On cash pricing that is roughly $300 to $800 a year, and on the full Medicare replacement schedule it reaches about $1,058 annually. Over five years that clears $5,000 on the high end, which is more than the AirCurve 11 VAuto, the most expensive machine on this list. This is why the standard 22mm hose fitting is the spec I check before anything else. The AirSense 11, AirSense 10, Luna G3, iBreeze, iX-Auto and prisma SMART max all take it, so their owners shop the whole mask market. The AirMini uses ResMed's own narrow tube with a short compatible mask list, and that constraint follows you for the life of the device.

highlights.title: The React Health Luna G3 is the machine I recommend to anyone who flinches at the ResMed price
highlights.body: The Luna G3 sells around $849 with the heated humidifier and integrated heated tubing already in the box, which is where the ResMed comparison gets interesting, because heated tubing is a paid add-on in most AirSense 11 configurations. It uses a standard 22mm hose fitting, so the mask market stays open. It writes full therapy data to an SD card you physically own and can read on a desktop, which matters more than it sounds when a supplier's cloud portal is the only other window into your own numbers. React Health picked up a large share of the users who left Philips after the recall, and the device has now been in that role long enough to have a real field record.

highlights.title: Zepbound is a legitimate option for sleep apnea, and the trial data points to using it alongside CPAP
highlights.body: The FDA approved Zepbound in December 2024 for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity, the first drug to carry that indication. SURMOUNT-OSA is worth reading closely before anyone treats it as a replacement for a machine. The apnea-hypopnea index dropped 25 to 29 events per hour against placebo, and 42% to 50% of participants reached remission or mild disease. The detail that gets left out of most coverage is the arm-by-arm result: the group already on CPAP dropped 29.3 events per hour while the drug-only group dropped 25.3. The strongest result in the trial came from using both. Talk it through with a sleep physician, because this is a prescribing decision and the answer depends on weight, AHI and how well you tolerate a mask.

zh-tw.commentary:
2026 年要挑陽壓呼吸器，我覺得得先講一件多數榜單到現在還沒寫進去的事。

Philips Respironics 從 2024 年 4 月 9 日同意判決生效那天起，就不能在美國賣新的 CPAP 跟 BiPAP，判決條款要跑滿五年、拿到 FDA 合規通知，公司才能向法院聲請解除，換算下來最快也要 2029 年。Philips 在 2020 年還握著美國睡眠呼吸中止裝置市場大約 37%，等於整個品類有三分之一直接從貨架上消失。所以你現在搜到的推薦文，如果第一名還掛著 DreamStation，那份名單描述的是兩年前就關掉的市場。我這份榜只放今天真的下得了單的機器。

第二件要講的是價格結構，這個品類的價格長得跟一般 3C 很不一樣。

美國那邊透過保險走 DME 通路，一台 AirSense 11 的帳面價常常開到 1,800 美元；同一台機器 ResMed 官方商店賣 1,054 美元，現金通路落在 900 到 1,100 美元。2026 年美國私人保險的平均自付額已經超過 1,700 美元，還沒用掉自付額的人，等於是照那個灌水過的價格全額付，而且還要一併扛順從性監測，每晚滿四小時、在指定期間內達到 70% 的夜數，數字掉下來保險方可以停付甚至把機器收回去。自費買反而把這兩件事都省掉。Medicare 是唯一反過來的情況，2026 年 Part B 自付額只有 283 美元，之後給付八成，符合資格的人走保險比較划算。

台灣這邊的結構更單純，健保不給付主機，整台自費，市面上自動型機種大概從兩萬多到五萬多都有。實際上我覺得台灣讀者最該注意的反而是後面那筆錢。面罩軟墊每兩到四週換一次，管路每三個月，拋棄式濾網每個月，濕化水盒每半年。照現金價算一年大概三百到八百美元，照 Medicare 的完整更換表換算差不多一年 1,058 美元，五年下來比這份榜上任何一台機器都貴。

所以我把管路接口跟面罩自由度的權重拉得很高。走標準 22mm 接口的機器，你可以在整個面罩市場裡挑，哪一款軟墊漏氣就換下一個牌子；用原廠專屬細管的機器，往後幾年的耗材錢就綁在同一家身上。

最後提醒一句，這類機器在美國一定要處方才能買，台灣也建議先做完睡眠檢查再決定。這一頁比的是產品、價格跟通路，壓力設定、模式選擇還有要不要用 Zepbound 這種問題，請帶去問睡眠專科醫師。

highlights.title: ResMed AirSense 11 拿第一，靠的是通路穩定跟面罩自由度
highlights.body: 我最後還是把 AirSense 11 放在第一，理由很實際，它把決定長期花費的那兩件事都做對了。第一是它走標準 22mm 管路接口，市面上的面罩幾乎都能接，哪天軟墊怎麼調都會漏氣，你當週就能換另一個牌子繼續用。第二是 ResMed 官方商店直接掛出 1,054 美元的現金價，這個數字給了所有人一個可以拿去對照經銷商報價的硬指標。AutoSet 演算法累積了十年的實際使用資料，myAir 每天早上把使用時數跟 AHI 推到手機，濕化器跟加熱管是同一組模組、只有兩條水路要洗。老實說，1,054 美元是我願意當作預設推薦的價格上限，而它比 599 美元那一級貴出來的部分，光是面罩生態系就補得回來。

highlights.title: 美國那邊自費買比走保險划算，而且差距不小；台灣則是從頭到尾都自費
highlights.body: 這段算術直接改變了我排這個品類的方式。美國經銷商走保險，一台 AirSense 11 的帳面價常見 1,800 美元；同一台 ResMed 官方賣 1,054 美元，現金通路 900 到 1,100 美元。2026 年私人保險平均自付額超過 1,700 美元，還沒用掉自付額的人就是照灌水價全額付。走保險還附帶順從性監測，每晚四小時、70% 的夜數，數字沒達標保險方可以停止給付甚至收回機器。自費買把價差跟監測一次解決。Medicare 是唯一的例外，Part B 自付額 283 美元、之後給付八成，有資格的人走保險才對。台灣的情況比較單純，健保不給付主機，你看到的標價就是你要付的錢，所以在台灣買，能不能自己驗證那個價格反而更重要。

highlights.title: 五年的軟墊跟管路比機器本身還貴，所以先看管路接口再看規格
highlights.body: 面罩軟墊每兩到四週換，管路每三個月，拋棄式濾網每個月，濕化水盒每半年。照現金價算一年三百到八百美元，照 Medicare 完整更換表算大約一年 1,058 美元，五年下來高標超過 5,000 美元，比這份榜上最貴的 AirCurve 11 VAuto 還多。這就是為什麼我看任何一台機器，第一個查的欄位是管路接口。AirSense 11、AirSense 10、Luna G3、iBreeze、iX-Auto 跟 prisma SMART max 全部走標準 22mm，這些機主可以在整個面罩市場裡自由挑選。AirMini 用的是 ResMed 自家細管，可搭配的面罩清單很短，這個限制會跟著你到換機為止。台灣的通路又更現實一點，冷門接口的耗材要等進貨，這一點在下單前就要問清楚。

highlights.title: 覺得 ResMed 太貴的人，我會直接推 React Health Luna G3
highlights.body: Luna G3 大概 849 美元，加熱濕化器跟整合式加熱管路都已經含在盒子裡，而加熱管路在 AirSense 11 多數配置裡是要另外加價的選項，所以兩台實際的價差比帳面上更大。它一樣走標準 22mm 接口，面罩市場整個對你開放。完整的治療數據會寫進你自己拿在手上的 SD 卡，插進電腦讀卡機就看得到，這件事聽起來小，實際上很重要，因為另一條看到自己數據的路是經銷商的雲端後台，那個後台什麼時候關、關了要不要收費，決定權都不在你身上。召回之後離開 Philips 的使用者大部分轉到這台，跑到現在也累積出足夠的實際使用回饋了。

highlights.title: Zepbound 是真的可以考慮的選項，而試驗數據指向的是跟 CPAP 併用
highlights.body: FDA 在 2024 年 12 月核准 Zepbound 用於併有肥胖的中重度阻塞型睡眠呼吸中止，這是第一個拿到這個適應症的藥物。不過 SURMOUNT-OSA 的內容值得仔細看完再決定。整體來說呼吸中止低通氣指數相對安慰劑下降了每小時 25 到 29 次，42% 到 50% 的受試者達到緩解或降為輕度，這個效果確實很紮實。多數報導漏掉的是分組結果，已經在用 CPAP 的那一組下降 29.3 次，單用藥物的那一組下降 25.3 次，試驗裡表現最好的組合是兩個一起用。這是處方決策，牽涉到體重、AHI 跟你戴面罩的耐受度，請帶著這些數字去跟睡眠專科醫師討論。台灣目前的取得管道跟給付狀況也要另外問診所確認。

en.commentary:
The ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet keeps first place at 9.3, and the ranking holds this week. It is an auto-adjusting CPAP with a built-in heated humidifier, a touchscreen and the myAir app, which shows your nightly usage, mask seal and events. The reason it stays on top ties directly to this week's research news.

At the European Respiratory Society Congress in Barcelona, held 5 to 9 September, ResMed presented research across the sleep apnea therapy journey. The headline was a late-breaking analysis of a French national database, presented by Prof. Jean-Louis Pépin, which found that each additional hour of nightly PAP use was associated with a lower risk of death among people with obstructive sleep apnea. This is observational data, so it shows an association. Even so, it reinforces the principle I build this ranking on: the best machine is the one you will wear for the whole night.

That is why comfort features and readable data carry so much weight in my scores. AirSense 11 makes nightly hours visible in myAir, and seeing that number every morning is a practical motivator.

The React Health Luna G3 holds second at 8.8. It is an auto CPAP with an integrated humidifier and standard tubing that accepts common masks, and its cash price of $849 makes it my value pick for a full-size machine. The ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet stays third at 8.6 as a proven workhorse.

The US market structure stays the same. Philips Respironics remains under its consent decree and cannot sell new sleep therapy devices in the United States, so this ranking reflects the machines you can actually buy.

If your usage is slipping, talk to your sleep clinician about mask fit before giving up. A different mask style often fixes the problem.

zh-tw.commentary:
這週 ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet 繼續以 9.3 分拿第一，排名沒變。它是自動調壓的正壓呼吸器，內建加熱加濕器、觸控螢幕，還能搭配 myAir App，每天看得到使用時數、面罩密合度和事件次數。它守住第一的理由，剛好跟這週的研究新聞直接相關。

en.commentary:
The ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet keeps first place at 9.3 and my ranking holds this week. It is an auto-adjusting CPAP with an integrated heated humidifier, a color touchscreen and the myAir app, which reports nightly hours, mask seal and residual events. It stays on top because it gives new users the most support during the first weeks, which is when most people give up.

That support is getting smarter. ResMed's Smart Comfort feature has FDA clearance as an AI-enabled tool that recommends personalized comfort settings, such as ramp and humidity, to help people start and stay on therapy. ResMed plans a broader US rollout to new myAir users later in 2026. Combined with the ERS 2026 analysis linking each extra nightly hour of PAP use to lower mortality, the logic is clear to me: a machine that keeps you wearing the mask longer is worth paying for.

I also want to address the pill headlines. AD109, an oral drug for obstructive sleep apnea, cut breathing events substantially in a phase 3 trial, with 18 percent of participants reaching complete disease control. That is promising research. It is still a candidate medication, and for anyone diagnosed today, CPAP remains the proven therapy your sleep physician will prescribe. Keep your machine on your nightstand and discuss new options at your next follow-up.

React Health Luna G3 holds second at 8.8 as the best value full-size machine, with a heated humidifier and cellular data included. The AirSense 10 stays third at 8.6 and often costs less where refurbished stock remains available.

In Taiwan, AirSense 11 is sold through licensed medical equipment dealers, so book a pressure trial and mask fitting before you commit to a purchase.

en.commentary:
React Health went quiet this week, and my ranking moves because of it. The company folded into AdaptHealth on 1 June 2026, reacthealth.com stopped resolving entirely, and retailers now carry the Luna G3 Auto CPAP with a discontinued-for-2026 label. I have moved it from second place to sixth and cut its availability score from 9.4 to 5.0.

I want to be precise about what changed. The Luna G3 is still the machine I described last week on engineering merit. It takes a standard 22mm hose, it writes full therapy data to an SD card you own, and closeout stock near $849 is real money saved. The factor it lost is the first one I score, which is what you can actually buy and keep running through 2026. A CPAP is a five to seven year commitment that leans on filters, firmware support and a warranty desk that picks up the phone. If you buy remaining stock, plan on sourcing supplies from third parties for the rest of the machine's life.

Transcend fills the gap. The Micro 510 Auto CPAP enters at fifth with 8.0. It weighs 0.48 pounds, runs at 27 dBA, and ships for $829 with a three year warranty, a hard shell case, hypoallergenic filters and the AirMist HME in the box. The detail that earns it 9.5 on mask freedom is the universal 22mm connection, so the mask you already own fits on the first night. Travel size combined with an open supply chain is a rare pairing, and it is why I place it above both travel machines below it.

My top four are otherwise steady. The AirSense 11 AutoSet holds first at 9.3, the AirSense 10 moves up to second at 8.6, and the Resvent iBreeze takes third at 8.3. For readers in Taiwan the Wellell iX-Auto at 8.1 stays the pragmatic answer, with local service and consumables you can buy in person. Talk to your clinician before you change pressure settings or mask style.

en.commentary:
The ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet keeps first at 9.3 and my ranking holds after last week's React Health shake-up. The news readers keep forwarding me is a sleep apnea pill, so let me put it in context for anyone deciding whether to buy a machine this autumn.

The drug is AD109, a nightly combination of aroxybutynin and atomoxetine that aims to keep throat muscles engaged so the airway stays open. In the phase 3 SynAIRgy trial, 646 adults at 69 sites who had refused or could not tolerate CPAP took it for six months. Their apnea-hypoxia index fell by about 44 percent, against 18 percent on placebo, and 18 percent of patients reached complete disease control. That is a meaningful result for people who have given up on a mask.

The trial's own lead author still calls CPAP the gold standard, and the numbers explain why. A machine used every night brings most patients' events down to a normal range, and it works regardless of what drives the collapse. My advice is this: if you have been diagnosed and your machine is tolerable, keep using it. If you have abandoned CPAP, bring this trial to your sleep physician and ask what it means for you.

Tolerance is what my scoring rewards. The AirSense 11 holds first on its quiet motor, integrated humidifier and a ramp that starts pressure gently, and the AirSense 10 at 8.6 delivers the same comfort features at a lower price. For readers in Taiwan's humid climate, a heated tube cuts rainout noticeably in winter.

Drugwatch counts 624 pending cases in the Philips CPAP litigation as of September 2026. That history is why manufacturer track record and supply continuity sit inside my availability score.

ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet 繼續第一，9.3 分，上週 React Health 那波調整之後，排名今天維持。最近讀者一直轉傳給我的新聞是睡眠呼吸中止症的口服藥，這邊幫正在考慮今年秋天要不要買機器的人整理一下。

這款藥叫 AD109，是 aroxybutynin 和 atomoxetine 的組合，每晚吃一次，目標是讓喉嚨肌肉維持張力，呼吸道比較不會塌陷。第三期 SynAIRgy 試驗在美國和加拿大 69 個地點收了 646 位成人，全部都是拒絕或受不了 CPAP 的患者，連續吃六個月。結果呼吸中止低血氧指數下降約 44%，安慰劑組是 18%，另外有 18% 的患者達到完全控制。對已經放棄戴面罩的人來說，這個結果很有意義。

不過試驗的第一作者自己也說，CPAP 仍然是黃金標準，數字就能解釋原因。每晚確實使用的機器，能讓大多數患者的事件數降到正常範圍，而且不管呼吸道塌陷的原因是什麼都有效。所以我的建議是：已經確診、機器也戴得習慣的人，繼續用。已經把機器收進櫃子的人，把這份試驗帶去給睡眠專科醫師，問問對你代表什麼。

我的評分本來就獎勵「戴得住」。AirSense 11 靠安靜的馬達、一體式加濕器和緩升壓力功能拿第一；AirSense 10 8.6 分，舒適功能差不多，價格更好入手。台灣濕氣重，冬天冷氣團一來管路很容易積水，加熱管真的差很多。

Drugwatch 統計到 2026 年 9 月，Philips CPAP 訴訟還有 624 件未結。這段歷史就是我把廠商紀錄和耗材供應穩定度放進可取得性分數的原因。
